repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend at main 4c2119da (tag 0.286.0); every path in `read` is relative to that repo root. The live-animals notification journey is one set, src/server/app/sets/live-animals, about 31,900 non-unit-test lines including src/server/app/shared. Its one journey style, journeys/linear, has 21 feature folders under journeys/linear/features (dashboard, hub, origin, commodities [search, consignment-details, animal-identification], import-reason, additional-details, documents, addresses [party-picker, party-edit, address-return], cph-number, transport [port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, transporter-add, transporters-select, commercial-transporter-details, private-transporter-details], contact, check-answers, declaration, confirmation, cancel-amend, notification-actions, delete-notification, system), each holding page.js, controller(s), Nunjucks templates, validate.js, view-model helpers, an English and a Welsh copy file and its *.fit.spec.js Playwright specs. The flow (journeys/linear/flow: ten sections start, origin, commodities, animalIdentification, consignment, documents, addresses, transport, contact, review) orders the pages; obligations/ (index.js and sections/*.js, about 1,000 lines) declares what each notification must hold, in scope and mandatory; services/commodities is the commodity reference service and its stub; docs/ holds the set's recipe and model docs. Shared layout and copy live in src/server/app/shared (layout.njk, kit.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, save-actions, error summary, section caption, set-context). The set is mounted by src/server/app/routes-live-animals.js. The repo's decisions ledger is src/server/app/docs/decisions.md (56 lines, architecture decisions, not product rulings); no rulings ledger such as spec/decisions.json exists. One repo-level fit spec, fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js, walks the whole journey. Cut into 14 parts by what a user sees: shared layout and flow, the obligation model and ledger, then one part per page group in journey order, with the dashboard and its notification actions as one part. Left out: every *.test.js unit test; the generic platform under src/server/app (engine, model, bridge, flow, lib, analysis, services other than address-book) beyond what a part names; src/server/common, auth and health; the characterisation and reachability fixtures (journeys/linear/fixtures, flow/fixtures, flow/reachability-fixtures), which are test data; coverage/ and build output. Welsh copy files are read for existence and parity only: claims quote the English copy.

Covered: the declaration page at /notifications/{id}/declaration (heading, five declaration statements with two bullet lists, the single 'confirmed' checkbox, the date of declaration line, Continue button, the required-checkbox error verbatim, back link to check answers, the already-submitted redirect, the review-refusal redirect, the recoverable save failure, and the commit plus submit to confirmation); the confirmation page at /notifications/{id}/confirmation (GET only, the redirect for an unsubmitted notification, the panel with title and reference number, the outstanding-documents section and when it shows, the transporting, view-or-amend and getting-help sections with every link and the create-a-new-notification POST button, no back link); Welsh copy parity for both pages (machine-draft); and every test in declaration.fit.spec.js (5 tests) and confirmation.fit.spec.js (5 tests). Unit tests (controller.test.js, template.test.js, copy.test.js) are outside the partition's scope and were not claimed.

claims.statement: Every animal-identifier record must carry at least one of: microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag or horse name; otherwise it fails with obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired.

missing ownership.

own labels, hints, options, validation messages and templates. Boot-time purity
checks reject display-shaped keys in the model.

## Composition is explicit

claims.statement: Platform limit: the obligation model is executable code (scope rules are functions), not portable JSON configuration.
claims.quote:
Obligation `applyTo` rules are JavaScript functions. Helper metadata makes their
dependencies inspectable, but the manifest is not portable JSON configuration.

claims.statement: Platform limit: a page's derived gate opens when at least one answer it collects is in scope and its prerequisites pass.
claims.quote:
The normal page gate passes when at least one collected obligation is in scope and
its prerequisites pass.

claims.statement: Platform limit: a list-valued answer (such as species) cannot drive a single-value scope gate; collection conditions use group-aware rules instead.
claims.quote:
The standard scalar gate helpers expect scalar fulfilment values. Collection
conditions use group-aware helpers and cardinality rules instead.

claims.statement: Platform limit: ownership of nested collection fields is derived from the collection root a page claims; no second page may own a nested field.
claims.quote: Do not declare a second page owner for a nested leaf.

claims.statement: Platform limit: saving is not transactional across backend projections; a partial failure is reported to the user as a recoverable backend error.
claims.quote:
Real persistence can update
more than one backend projection, and adapter code is responsible for reporting
partial failures as recoverable backend errors.

After a removal the user returns to the Commodity details page while any line is left, or to the commodity search page when the last line was removed (keeping the change context).
Removing a commodity also removes any animal identifier records held on its lines, because the whole line is dropped.

claims.note: Identifier records are stored under each line (evaluation.js groups unit under line), so dropping the line drops them. No confirmation step is shown before removal.

claims.statement: A return with a fulfilment id that matches no party is rejected as a bad request ('Unknown fulfilment').
A return with no address id sends the trader to the party's picker without saving anything.
A return whose handshake token does not match the one remembered for that fulfilment id is rejected as a bad request ('Invalid handshake').
A verified handshake token is used once: it is cleared, and the cookie is removed when no tokens remain.
The returned address id is looked up in the signed-in organisation's own address book, so an id from another organisation is treated as not found.
If the address book cannot be reached on return, the trader goes to the picker with the 'unavailable' handshake error.
If the returned address is not found or is soft-deleted, the trader goes to the picker with the 'not-found' handshake error.
A good return stores a copy of the returned address as that party's answer, exactly as a picker selection would.
If saving the returned address fails, the trader goes to the picker with the 'unavailable' handshake error.
